cards.text: Isaiah, the LORD's prophet, has just described priests and prophets who stagger from wine and scoff at the LORD's message (Isaiah 28:7-13). Now the word of the LORD comes for the scoffers who rule the people in Jerusalem, because they said, "We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol." Out of EVERYBODY in the world to sign a deal with, they picked DEATH.

cards.question: The rulers in Jerusalem say they've made a deal with death and Sheol. What do they think it gets them?

answers.text: The scourge will not touch them

cards.text: Then they say what their safety rests on, right out loud: "because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place." Friend, that's putting tape over the check engine light and calling the car FIXED.
So the Lord GOD answers them. But before He says a word about their hiding place, He talks about a stone He's laying.

cards.question: The Lord GOD is speaking to the rulers in Jerusalem. He says He's laying a stone in ___.
The Lord GOD calls His stone a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. He says the one who believes will never be shaken.

cards.text: Hold on to this stone, friend. Peter quotes this very line in his first letter and points it to Jesus (1 Peter 2:4-7).
Then the Lord GOD says, "I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level." When God holds a level up to your wall, there is no "eh, close enough."

cards.question: The rulers are hiding in a refuge of lies. What does the Lord GOD say will sweep it away?
The Lord GOD says the rulers' covenant with death will still stand when trouble comes.
The rulers were sure the overwhelming scourge would pass them by. The Lord GOD says that when it passes through, they will be ___ by it.

cards.text: And it won't come just once. It will carry them away, sweeping through morning after morning, by day and by night, and Isaiah says understanding this message will bring sheer terror.

Then Isaiah gives a picture from everyday life: "the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under a pile of old paper, and NOT ONE takeout menu ever covered my whole mustache.

Then Isaiah says the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim and rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon. At Baal-perazim, the LORD burst out against David's enemies like a bursting flood (2 Samuel 5:20).

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD will rise up to do His work and perform His task. How does Isaiah describe that work and that task?
Isaiah warns the scoffers to stop mocking. If they don't, what does he say will happen to their shackles?
Isaiah has heard a decree of destruction from the Lord GOD of Hosts. It's against the whole ___.

cards.text: Now Isaiah says, "Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say." And then the prophet does something nobody saw coming: he starts talking about FARMING.

cards.question: Isaiah asks, "Does the plowman plow for planting every day?" Does he just keep loosening the soil forever? What answer is Isaiah after?

answers.text: No once it's level he plants
Yes he plows all year long
Yes the soil always needs more

cards.text: Once the ground is leveled, the farmer sows caraway and scatters cumin. Plowing every day forever? That's me preheating the oven for three weeks and calling myself a BAKER.

cards.question: Isaiah says the farmer throws his wheat, barley and rye all together into one big pile of seed.
Caraway and cumin scattered, wheat in rows, barley in plots, rye within its border. Isaiah says the farmer knows how because his ___ instructs and teaches him properly.

cards.text: Then comes the harvest. Isaiah says caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and a cart wheel is not rolled over the cumin.

cards.question: The farmer doesn't use a threshing sledge on his caraway. What does he beat it out with instead?

cards.text: A stick for the caraway and a rod for the cumin. Different seed, different tool, the same way you don't press a delicate sugar cookie with a sledgehammer, and friend, I have the FLAT cookie to prove it.

cards.question: Isaiah says grain for bread is threshed over and over until the horses crush it.

cards.text: Right. Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed, and though the cart wheels roll over it, the horses do not crush it.

cards.question: Isaiah wraps up the farming picture. Where does he say all this also comes from?

cards.text: Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts is "wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom." Friend, the God who taught that farmer when to stop plowing is NOT winging it.

findings.problem: The opening card says the priests and prophets who stagger from wine also 'scoff at the LORD's message (Isaiah 28:7-13).' Isaiah 28:7-8 describes the staggering priests and prophets. The mocking words in 28:9-10 have no named speaker, so the card links two things the text leaves unlinked. It also applies 'scoff' to a group the text never calls scoffers. In 28:14 the scoffers are the rulers in Jerusalem.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card only points ahead to 1 Peter 2:4-7. It tells no part of Isaiah 28 and doesn't move the baker forward through the passage. The 1 Peter connection is allowed as an outside fact with its reference, but it should ride along on a card that also carries a moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Isaiah 28:21 says 'Mount Perazim.' The card follows it with what happened 'At Baal-perazim' (2 Samuel 5:20), which presents the two places as the same. Neither text says they are the same place.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The card says the prophet 'starts talking about FARMING.' That is the content of Isaiah 28:24, but the card cites only Isaiah 28:23.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only one that starts with 'No.' Both wrong answers start with 'Yes' and say nearly the same thing. A baker can pick the odd one out without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This card mostly repeats the answer the baker just gave on card 9 (grain is not endlessly threshed and the horses do not crush it), so it works as a recap. It also opens with 'Right.' which assumes the baker answered correctly, even though they may have picked True.
